conventions.convention: p ≥ 4 is even; A is primitive of order 2p; r=p/2; δ=−A²−A⁻²; q=−A²; quantum integers satisfy [0]=0, [1]=1 and [j+1]=δ[j]−[j−1]. The retained labels are 0,…,r−2.
Negligibility uses the unnormalized planar closure pairing against every reverse morphism. The category is then completed by finite direct sums and splitting idempotents.
The BHMV ribbon convention uses crossing A·1+A⁻¹U, planar dimensions d_a=[a+1], and twists θ_a=(−1)^a A^{a(a+2)}. It differs from the positive-pivotal quantum convention by tensor parity.
κ is a sixth root satisfying κ⁶=A^{−6−(p+1)p/2}. Composition adds the Wall-sign Maslov index in the order (Λ_M1(λ0), λ1, Λ_M2ᵗ(λ2)). One weight step acts by ν=κ³.
The pairing uses the TQFT normalization Z_p(M,Γ,w)=η^{b0(M)+b1(M)}(κ³)^w θ_p(M,Γ), rather than raw signature-normalized θ_p. In particular Z_p(S³,∅,0)=η and Z_p(S²×S¹,∅,0)=1.

load_bearing.statement: The complete simple-label set is {0,…,r−2}; every simple is self-dual. N_ab^c=1 exactly when |a−b|≤c≤min(a+b,2r−4−a−b) and a+b+c is even, and is zero otherwise. In the stated BHMV ribbon convention the dimensions are [a+1], the twists are (−1)^a A^{a(a+2)}, and the unnormalized Hopf-link matrix is nondegenerate.
For the specified marking and anomaly data, V_p(Σ) is the colored relative handlebody skein module modulo the left radical of the normalized complementary-handlebody pairing.

The normalized BHMV sesquilinear pairing between complementary marked handlebody skein modules induces a perfect pairing between their radical quotients, using the coefficient-conjugate space on the oppositely oriented side. Its inverse defines sewing, with the stated weighted Lagrangian anomaly correction.

For the fixed even root, both Gauss sums Δ_± are nonzero, and the Ω_p-colored bracket divided by Δ_+^{b_+}Δ_-^{b_-} is invariant under framed isotopy, handle slides, and split ±1-framed unknot addition or deletion.
For even p≥4 and primitive A of order 2p, the negligible tensor ideal at loop value −A²−A⁻² is generated by p_{r−1}; the surviving projector labels are precisely 0,…,r−2.

concerns.concern: The Definition instructs one to glue x and y from two ordinary complex skein modules, sets B_Σ(x,y)=Z_p(S³,Γ,w), and then declares this conjugate-linear in y. Ordinary gluing and evaluation are complex-linear in both skein inputs: for empty skeins in complementary balls, the displayed construction gives B(∅,i∅)=iη, whereas the declared sesquilinearity requires −iη, with η≠0. An explicit semilinear orientation-reversal/conjugation map on the second input is missing. BHMV Proposition 1.9, p.891, uses M glued to −M′ and reverses the second link; §5.8, pp.912–913, expressly distinguishes this sesquilinear pairing from the complementary bilinear pairing. Clarify the actual domains and reversal before using the coefficient-conjugate space and inverse tensor in the pairing lemma.

The Definition permits a general closed marked surface Σ but requires complementary handlebodies whose gluing is the standard S³. This construction covers connected surfaces; it does not specify state spaces for disconnected surfaces or the empty surface, both of which occur in the stated weighted symmetric monoidal bordism category. BHMV Proposition 1.9 requires connected filling manifolds, and its complementary-handlebody example explicitly assumes connected Σ. The componentwise tensor-product construction and V_p(∅)=C need to be stated or explicitly imported before the final theorem claims a TQFT on the entire category.

alerts.finding: The published Definition says that 'the right-hand cup-cap is U_r'. Its TikZ paths from (2,0) and (3,0) both end at (2.5,0.9), and two further paths run from that same point to (2,1.8) and (3,1.8). Thus four arcs meet at a single interior point, rather than forming the two disjoint cup/cap arcs of a Temperley–Lieb matching. An additional vertical strand at x=2 also overlaps this supposed generator. The drawing does not depict U_r or the displayed recursive composite; the algebraic formula itself is independent of the drawing.

seams_checked.note: The final theorem uses the opened Kirby-classification statement for finite integral framed links in standard oriented S³, retaining full AC and precisely isotopy, fully framed slides, and split ±1-unknot moves. No stronger marked-bordism classification is attributed to that theorem.

The opened skein-module Definition supplies the same crossing smoothings, loop value, framed isotopy, and empty-link convention. The opened solid-torus theorem supplies the prequotient core-multicurve basis under AC; the worked example correctly obtains its finite torus dimension from the separate BHMV quotient-basis input.
